2  	title: Font Optimization
3  	description: Learn how to optimize fonts in Next.js
4  	related:
5  	  title: API Reference
6  	  description: See the API Reference for the full feature set of Next.js Font
7  	  links:
8  	    - app/api-reference/components/font
9  	---
10 	
11 	The [`next/font`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/font) module automatically optimizes your fonts and removes external network requests for improved privacy and performance.
12 	
13 	It includes **built-in self-hosting** for any font file. This means you can optimally load web fonts with no layout shift.
14 	
15 	<AppOnly>
16 	
17 	To start using `next/font`, import it from [`next/font/local`](#local-fonts) or [`next/font/google`](#google-fonts), call it as a function with the appropriate options, and set the `className` of the element you want to apply the font to. For example:
18 	
19 	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" highlight={1,3-5,9} switcher
20 	import { Geist } from 'next/font/google'
21 	
22 	const geist = Geist({
23 	  subsets: ['latin'],
24 	})
25 	
26 	export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
27 	  return (
28 	    <html lang="en" className={geist.className}>
29 	      <body>{children}</body>
30 	    </html>
31 	  )
32 	}
33 	```
34 	
35 	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" highlight={1,3-5,9} switcher
36 	import { Geist } from 'next/font/google'
37 	
38 	const geist = Geist({
39 	  subsets: ['latin'],
40 	})
41 	
42 	export default function Layout({ children }) {
43 	  return (
44 	    <html className={geist.className}>
45 	      <body>{children}</body>
46 	    </html>
47 	  )
48 	}
49 	```
50 	
51 	Fonts are scoped to the component they're used in. To apply a font to your entire application, add it to the [Root Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout).
52 	
53 	</AppOnly>

1  	---
2  	title: Revalidating
3  	description: Learn how to revalidate cached data using time-based and on-demand strategies.
4  	related:
5  	  title: API Reference
6  	  description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned on this page.
7  	  links:
8  	    - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife
9  	    - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag
10 	    - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag
11 	    - app/api-reference/functions/updateTag
12 	    - app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath
13 	---
14 	
15 	> This page covers revalidation with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.
16 	
17 	Revalidation is the process of updating cached data. It lets you keep serving fast, cached responses while ensuring content stays fresh. There are two strategies:
18 	
19 	- **Time-based revalidation**: Automatically refresh cached data after a set duration using [`cacheLife`](#cachelife).
20 	- **On-demand revalidation**: Manually invalidate cached data after a mutation using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag), [`updateTag`](#updatetag), or [`revalidatePath`](#revalidatepath).
21 	
22 	## `cacheLife`
23 	
24 	[`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) controls how long cached data remains valid. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope to set the cache lifetime.
25 	
26 	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
27 	import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
28 	
29 	export async function getProducts() {
30 	  'use cache'
31 	  cacheLife('hours')
32 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
33 	}
34 	```
35 	
36 	`cacheLife` accepts a profile name or a custom configuration object:
37 	
38 	| Profile   | `stale` | `revalidate` | `expire` |
39 	| --------- | ------- | ------------ | -------- |
40 	| `default` | 5m      | 15m          | never    |
41 	| `seconds` | 30s     | 1s           | 60s      |
42 	| `minutes` | 5m      | 1m           | 1h       |
43 	| `hours`   | 5m      | 1h           | 1d       |
44 	| `days`    | 5m      | 1d           | 1w       |
45 	| `weeks`   | 5m      | 1w           | 30d      |
46 	| `max`     | 5m      | 30d          | 1y       |
47 	
48 	For fine-grained control, pass an object:
49 	
50 	```tsx highlight={2-6}
51 	'use cache'
52 	cacheLife({
53 	  stale: 3600, // 1 hour until considered stale
54 	  revalidate: 7200, // 2 hours until revalidated
55 	  expire: 86400, // 1 day until expired
56 	})
57 	```
58 	
59 	> **Good to know:** A cache is considered "short-lived" when it uses the `seconds` profile, `revalidate: 0`, or `expire` under 5 minutes. Short-lived caches are automatically excluded from prerenders and become dynamic holes instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for details.
60 	
61 	See the [`cacheLife` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) for all profiles and custom configuration options.
62 	
63 	## `cacheTag`
64 	
65 	[`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) lets you tag cached data so it can be invalidated on-demand. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope:
66 	
67 	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
68 	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
69 	
70 	export async function getProducts() {
71 	  'use cache'
72 	  cacheTag('products')
73 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
74 	}
75 	```
76 	
77 	```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
78 	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
79 	
80 	export async function getProducts() {
81 	  'use cache'
82 	  cacheTag('products')
83 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
84 	}
85 	```
86 	
87 	Once tagged, invalidate the cache using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag) or [`updateTag`](#updatetag).
88 	
89 	See the [`cacheTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) to learn more.
90 	
91 	## `revalidateTag`
92 	
93 	`revalidateTag` invalidates cache entries by tag using stale-while-revalidate semantics — stale content is served immediately while fresh content loads in the background. This is ideal for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, like blog posts or product catalogs.
94 	
95 	```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,5} switcher
96 	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
97 	
98 	export async function updateUser(id: string) {
99 	  // Mutate data
100	  revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate
101	}
102	```
103	
104	```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
105	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
106	
107	export async function updateUser(id) {
108	  // Mutate data
109	  revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate
110	}
111	```
112	
113	You can reuse the same tag in multiple functions to revalidate them all at once. Call `revalidateTag` in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
114	
115	> **Good to know:** The second argument sets how long stale content can be served while fresh content generates in the background. Once it expires, subsequent requests block until fresh content is ready. Using `'max'` gives the longest stale window.
116	
117	See the [`revalidateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to learn more.
118	
119	## `updateTag`
120	
121	`updateTag` immediately expires cached data for read-your-own-writes scenarios — the user sees their change right away instead of stale content. Unlike `revalidateTag`, it can only be used in [Server Actions](/docs/app/guides/server-actions).
122	
123	```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,12} switcher
124	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
125	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
126	
127	export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
128	  const post = await db.post.create({
129	    data: {
130	      title: formData.get('title'),
131	      content: formData.get('content'),
132	    },
133	  })
134	
135	  updateTag('posts')
136	  redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
137	}
138	```
139	
140	```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,12} switcher
141	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
142	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
143	
144	export async function createPost(formData) {
145	  const post = await db.post.create({
146	    data: {
147	      title: formData.get('title'),
148	      content: formData.get('content'),
149	    },
150	  })
151	
152	  updateTag('posts')
153	  redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
154	}
155	```
156	
157	|              | `updateTag`                                   | `revalidateTag`                      |
158	| ------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
159	| **Where**    | Server Actions only                           | Server Actions and Route Handlers    |
160	| **Behavior** | Immediately expires cache                     | Stale-while-revalidate               |
161	| **Use case** | Read-your-own-writes (user sees their change) | Background refresh (slight delay OK) |
162	
163	See the [`updateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) to learn more.
164	
165	## `revalidatePath`
166	
167	`revalidatePath` invalidates all cached data for a specific route path. Use it when you want to revalidate a route without knowing which tags are associated with it.
168	
169	```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,5} switcher
170	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
171	
172	export async function updateUser(id: string) {
173	  // Mutate data
174	  revalidatePath('/profile')
175	}
176	```
177	
178	```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
179	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
180	
181	export async function updateUser(id) {
182	  // Mutate data
183	  revalidatePath('/profile')
184	}
185	```
186	
187	> **Good to know**: Prefer tag-based revalidation (`revalidateTag`/`updateTag`) over path-based when possible — it's more precise and avoids over-invalidating.
188	
189	See the [`revalidatePath` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) to learn more.
190	
191	## What should I cache?
192	
193	Cache data that doesn't depend on [runtime data](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#working-with-runtime-apis) and that you're OK serving from cache for a period of time. Use `use cache` with `cacheLife` to describe that behavior.
194	
195	When content doesn't need time-based revalidation, for example data from a CMS, use [`cacheTag`](#cachetag) and a long [`cacheLife`](#cachelife) like `max` to keep it in the static shell. Configure the content source to trigger a webhook, or other notification, that calls [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag) when the content changes. This reduces unnecessary time-based revalidation for content that hasn't changed.
196	
197	> **Good to know:** In serverless environments, in-memory cache entries may not persist across revalidations. See [runtime caching considerations](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#runtime-caching-considerations) for details.
</content>

2  	title: generateStaticParams
3  	description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
4  	---
5  	
6  	The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
7  	
8  	`generateStaticParams` can be used with:
9  	
10 	- [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
11 	- [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
12 	- [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
13 	
14 	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
15 	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
16 	export async function generateStaticParams() {
17 	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
18 	
19 	  return posts.map((post) => ({
20 	    slug: post.slug,
21 	  }))
22 	}
23 	
24 	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
25 	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
26 	export default async function Page({
27 	  params,
28 	}: {
29 	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
30 	}) {
31 	  const { slug } = await params
32 	  // ...
33 	}
34 	```
35 	
36 	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
37 	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
38 	export async function generateStaticParams() {
39 	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
40 	
41 	  return posts.map((post) => ({
42 	    slug: post.slug,
43 	  }))
44 	}
45 	
46 	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
47 	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
48 	export default async function Page({ params }) {
49 	  const { slug } = await params
50 	  // ...
51 	}
52 	```
53 	
54 	> **Good to know**:
55 	>
56 	> - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
57 	> - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
58 	> - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
59 	> - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
60 	> - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
61 	> - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
62 	
63 	## Parameters
64 	
65 	`options.params` (optional)
66 	
67 	If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
68 	
69 	The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
70 	
71 	## Returns
72 	
73 	`generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
74 	
75 	- Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
76 	- The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.
77 	
78 	| Example Route                    | `generateStaticParams` Return Type        |
79 	| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
80 	| `/product/[id]`                  | `{ id: string }[]`                        |
81 	| `/products/[category]/[product]` | `{ category: string, product: string }[]` |
82 	| `/products/[...slug]`            | `{ slug: string[] }[]`                    |
83 	
84 	## Single Dynamic Segment
85 	
86 	```tsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
87 	export function generateStaticParams() {
88 	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
89 	}
90 	
91 	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
92 	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
93 	// - /product/1
94 	// - /product/2
95 	// - /product/3
96 	export default async function Page({
97 	  params,
98 	}: {
99 	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
100	}) {
101	  const { id } = await params
102	  // ...
103	}
104	```
105	
106	```jsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.js" switcher
107	export function generateStaticParams() {
108	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
109	}
110	
111	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
112	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
113	// - /product/1
114	// - /product/2
115	// - /product/3
116	export default async function Page({ params }) {
117	  const { id } = await params
118	  // ...
119	}
120	```
121	
122	## Multiple Dynamic Segments
123	
124	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher

126	  return [

128	    { category: 'b', product: '2' },

4  	---
5  	
6  	Route Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.
7  	
8  	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
9  	export async function GET() {
10 	  return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })
11 	}
12 	```
13 	
14 	```js filename="route.js" switcher
15 	export async function GET() {
16 	  return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })
17 	}
18 	```
19 	
20 	## Reference
21 	
22 	### HTTP Methods
23 	
24 	A **route** file allows you to create custom request handlers for a given route. The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`.
25 	
26 	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
27 	export async function GET(request: Request) {}
28 	
29 	export async function HEAD(request: Request) {}
30 	
31 	export async function POST(request: Request) {}
32 	
33 	export async function PUT(request: Request) {}
34 	
35 	export async function DELETE(request: Request) {}
36 	
37 	export async function PATCH(request: Request) {}
38 	
39 	// If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.
40 	export async function OPTIONS(request: Request) {}
41 	```
42 	
43 	```js filename="route.js" switcher
44 	export async function GET(request) {}
45 	
46 	export async function HEAD(request) {}
47 	
48 	export async function POST(request) {}
49 	
50 	export async function PUT(request) {}
51 	
52 	export async function DELETE(request) {}
53 	
54 	export async function PATCH(request) {}
55 	
56 	// If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.
57 	export async function OPTIONS(request) {}
58 	```
59 	
60 	### Parameters
61 	
62 	#### `request` (optional)
63 	
64 	The `request` object is a [NextRequest](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) object, which is an extension of the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) API. `NextRequest` gives you further control over the incoming request, including easily accessing `cookies` and an extended, parsed, URL object `nextUrl`.
65 	
66 	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
67 	import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
68 	
69 	export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
70 	  const url = request.nextUrl
71 	}
72 	```
73 	
74 	```js filename="route.js" switcher
75 	export async function GET(request) {
76 	  const url = request.nextUrl
77 	}
78 	```
79 	
80 	#### `context` (optional)
81 	
82 	- **`params`**: a promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) for the current route.
83 	
84 	```ts filename="app/dashboard/[team]/route.ts" switcher
85 	export async function GET(
86 	  request: Request,
87 	  { params }: { params: Promise<{ team: string }> }
88 	) {
89 	  const { team } = await params
90 	}
91 	```
92 	
93 	```js filename="app/dashboard/[team]/route.js" switcher
94 	export async function GET(request, { params }) {
95 	  const { team } = await params
96 	}
97 	```

100	| -------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
101	| `app/dashboard/[team]/route.js`  | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>`           |
102	| `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/route.js` | `/shop/1/2`    | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` |
103	| `app/blog/[...slug]/route.js`    | `/blog/1/2`    | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>`    |
104

106	
107	You can type the Route Handler context using `RouteContext` to get strongly typed `params` from a route literal. `RouteContext` is a globally available helper.

113	  const { id } = await ctx.params
114	  return Response.json({ id })

116	```

9 	---
10	
11	The `notFound` function throws an error that renders a Next.js 404 page. It's useful for handling missing resources in your application. You can customize the UI using the [`not-found.js` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found).
12	
13	Invoking `notFound()` throws a `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404` error and terminates rendering of the route segment where it was thrown. Next.js also injects a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` tag so the page is not indexed. Because it works by throwing, call it in the render path: a component, or a function a component `await`s. A call left in an un-awaited promise throws where nothing catches it, and no not-found UI renders (in development the server logs `⨯ unhandledRejection: NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404`).
14	
15	`notFound()` can be invoked in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data), and [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
16	
17	```tsx filename="app/user/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
18	import { notFound } from 'next/navigation'
19	
20	async function fetchUser(id: string) {
21	  const res = await fetch('https://...')
22	  if (!res.ok) return undefined
23	  return res.json()
24	}
25	
26	export default async function Profile({
27	  params,
28	}: {
29	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
30	}) {
31	  const { id } = await params
32	  const user = await fetchUser(id)
33	
34	  if (!user) {
35	    notFound()
36	  }
37	
38	  // ...
39	}
40	```
41	
42	```jsx filename="app/user/[id]/page.js" switcher
43	import { notFound } from 'next/navigation'
44	
45	async function fetchUser(id) {
46	  const res = await fetch('https://...')

49	}
50

52	  const { id } = await params
53	  const user = await fetchUser(id)
54	
55	  if (!user) {
56	    notFound()
57	  }
58	
59	  // ...
60	}

1  	---
2  	title: layout.js
3  	description: API reference for the layout.js file.
4  	---
5  	
6  	The `layout` file is used to define a layout in your Next.js application.
7  	
8  	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" switcher
9  	export default function DashboardLayout({
10 	  children,
11 	}: {
12 	  children: React.ReactNode
13 	}) {
14 	  return <section>{children}</section>
15 	}
16 	```
17 	
18 	```jsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.js" switcher
19 	export default function DashboardLayout({ children }) {
20 	  return <section>{children}</section>
21 	}
22 	```
23 	
24 	In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `layout.js` is the outermost component in a route segment. It wraps `template.js`, `error.js`, `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, and `page.js`.
25 	
26 	A **root layout** is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. It is used to define the `<html>` and `<body>` tags and other globally shared UI.
27 	
28 	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
29 	export default function RootLayout({
30 	  children,
31 	}: {
32 	  children: React.ReactNode
33 	}) {
34 	  return (
35 	    <html lang="en">
36 	      <body>{children}</body>
37 	    </html>
38 	  )
39 	}
40 	```
41 	
42 	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
43 	export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
44 	  return (
45 	    <html lang="en">
46 	      <body>{children}</body>
47 	    </html>
48 	  )
49 	}
50 	```
51 	
52 	## Reference
53 	
54 	### Props
55 	
56 	#### `children` (required)
57 	
58 	Layout components should accept and use a `children` prop. During rendering, `children` will be populated with the route segments the layout is wrapping. These will primarily be the component of a child [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (if it exists) or [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), but could also be other special files like [Loading](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) or [Error](/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling) when applicable.
59 	
60 	#### `params` (optional)
61 	
62 	A promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to that layout.
63 	
64 	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.tsx" switcher
65 	export default async function Layout({
66 	  children,
67 	  params,
68 	}: {
69 	  children: React.ReactNode
70 	  params: Promise<{ team: string }>
71 	}) {
72 	  const { team } = await params
73 	}
74 	```
75 	
76 	```jsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js" switcher
77 	export default async function Layout({ children, params }) {
78 	  const { team } = await params
79 	}
80 	```
81 	
82 	| Example Route                     | URL            | `params`                           |
83 	| --------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
84 	| `app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js`  | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>`           |
85 	| `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/layout.js` | `/shop/1/2`    | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` |
86 	| `app/blog/[...slug]/layout.js`    | `/blog/1/2`    | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>`    |
87 	
88 	- Since the `params` prop is a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values.
89 	  - In version 14 and earlier, `params` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.
90 	
91 	### Layout Props Helper
92

2 	title: generateMetadata
3 	description: Learn how to add Metadata to your Next.js application for improved search engine optimization (SEO) and web shareability.
4 	related:
5 	  title: Next Steps
6 	  description: View all the Metadata API options.
7 	  links:
8 	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata
9 	    - app/api-reference/functions/generate-viewport
10	    - app/getting-started/caching
11	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
12	---
13	
14	You can use the `metadata` object or the `generateMetadata` function to define metadata.
15	
16	## The `metadata` object
17	
18	To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields) from a `layout.js` or `page.js` file.
19	
20	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
21	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
22	
23	export const metadata: Metadata = {
24	  title: '...',
25	  description: '...',
26	}
27	
28	export default function Page() {}
29	```
30	
31	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher
32	export const metadata = {
33	  title: '...',
34	  description: '...',
35	}
36	
37	export default function Page() {}
38	```
39	
40	> See the [Metadata Fields](#metadata-fields) for a complete list of supported options.
41	
42	## `generateMetadata` function
43	
44	Dynamic metadata depends on **dynamic information**, such as the current route parameters, external data, or `metadata` in parent segments, can be set by exporting a `generateMetadata` function that returns a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields).
45	
46	Resolving `generateMetadata` is part of rendering the page. If the page can be prerendered and `generateMetadata` doesn't introduce dynamic behavior, the resulting metadata is included in the page's initial HTML.
47	
48	Otherwise the metadata resolved from `generateMetadata` [can be streamed](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#streaming-metadata) after sending the initial UI.
49	
50	```tsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
51	import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
52	
53	type Props = {
54	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
55	  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
56	}
57	
58	export async function generateMetadata(
59	  { params, searchParams }: Props,
60	  parent: ResolvingMetadata
61	): Promise<Metadata> {
62	  // read route params
63	  const { id } = await params
64	
65	  // fetch data
66	  const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
67	
68	  // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
69	  const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
70	
71	  return {
72	    title: product.title,
73	    openGraph: {
74	      images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],
75	    },
76	  }
77	}
78	
79	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
80	```

events.content:
The Pages Router is gone. Every route now lives in app, and pages has been removed.

- _app and _document became app/layout.tsx. The root layout owns html and body, the shared shell, metadata, and Inter through next/font.
- next/head is replaced by the Metadata API. Dynamic post titles use generateMetadata.
- The home page is request-time rendered with headers() and connection(), replacing getServerSideProps.
- The blog index uses revalidate = 60. The post page uses generateStaticParams, dynamicParams, and revalidate = 300, replacing getStaticPaths and fallback: 'blocking'. Missing posts call notFound().
- 404 is app/not-found.tsx. _error is app/error.tsx plus app/global-error.tsx, using the retry prop instead of reset.
- API handlers are Route Handlers at app/api/posts/route.ts and app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts, with async params and Web Responses.
- Client navigation uses useRouter from next/navigation. Shared types are in lib/types.ts.

npx tsc --noEmit passed with exit code 0. npx next build passed with exit code 0: / is dynamic, /blog revalidates every minute, and the first 10 /blog/[id] paths are statically generated with a 5-minute revalidate.
